headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from AutoGen-to-Plane file/workspace handoff; capability conflict is limited by Plane's no-write profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write files, execute shell code, and run multi-agent tool calls; Plane accepts file uploads and handles notes/issues. If AutoGen outputs attacker-controlled content into a shared workspace or uploaded file, Plane may ingest it as trusted task content. Plane lacks a documented provenance filter, so the interaction is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF AutoGen writes prompt-like text into a shared file or upload consumed by Plane, injection is plausible.
IF Plane treats uploaded file contents as authoritative task text, attacker instructions can propagate.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for the two agents.
Disable automatic ingestion of uploaded files into task fields.
Add a manual review step before Plane imports AutoGen outputs.
Prefix AutoGen outputs with non-executable delimiters.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on all cross-agent artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen touches application data and model-provider API keys, with broad network egress and filesystem access; Plane touches issues, tasks, roadmaps, files, images, hyperlinks, and notes, and supports file uploads. A shared workspace or handoff can expose sensitive application data from AutoGen to Plane outputs or uploads. The profiles do not show isolation by default, so leakage is plausible.
conditions: IF both agents share a directory or upload channel, AutoGen-readable data can flow into Plane.
IF Plane stores uploaded files alongside issues or notes, sensitive content may persist beyond the original context.
mitigations: Keep separate directories and credentials.
Restrict Plane uploads to sanitized artifacts only.
Remove secrets from AutoGen working files before handoff.
Set short retention on uploaded attachments.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls on shared storage.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while Plane cannot write the filesystem per profile. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The remaining overlap is mostly read/network interaction, so contention exists only if an external orchestrator maps Plane uploads into writable shared storage.
conditions: IF an orchestrator grants Plane write access outside its profile, write conflict risk increases.
IF both agents target the same mutable directory through external tooling, contention can occur.
mitigations: Do not mount the same writable directory into both agents.
Keep Plane in read-only integration mode.
Serialize any shared-file updates.
Audit orchestrator permissions before launch.

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen can generate code, shell actions, and multi-agent outputs; Plane manages issues and tasks that may be acted on downstream. If Plane consumes AutoGen output without verification, errors or hallucinated facts can cascade into task creation or scheduling decisions. Plane's profile shows no built-in verification gate, so the handoff is risky in default workflows.
conditions: IF Plane imports AutoGen-generated text directly into tasks or issues, unverified errors can propagate.
IF downstream automation acts on Plane items created from AutoGen output, the cascade widens.
mitigations: Require human review before creating Plane tasks from AutoGen output.
Add a verification checklist for all imported facts.
Separate draft and approved queues in Plane.
Log source links for every imported item.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking before task creation.

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen handles model-provider API keys and broad application data, while Plane touches issues, tasks, files, images, and notes and offers file uploads plus external contact channels. The profiles do not specify residency, retention, or DPA controls, so compliance mismatch is plausible if regulated data is moved between them. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Plane uploads or issues, retention and residency obligations may apply.
IF AutoGen processes secrets or sensitive application data and forwards them into Plane, policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Block regulated data from cross-agent handoffs.
Document retention rules for Plane attachments.
Use redaction before exporting AutoGen artifacts.
Confirm residency and DPA terms before deployment.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data classification filters.
